answer.answer: PVE34 was the best practical profile for the old fixed-shape Nyx tuning regime, but later autonomy evidence superseded “PVE34 plus shorter chunks” as the operating model. The parser should now choose fetch, batch, and DB-lane settings from live pressure evidence, with learned priors and reversible trials. The next safe experiment is a bounded production-style alpha soak using that autonomous policy, full integrity gates, and explicit restart-recovery proof—not another fixed PVE34 optimization pass.

claims.value: Historical 10M checkpoint: run `split-lanes-64f-pve34-pvp2-other1-200k-to10m-20260523T115711Z` inserted `210624` rows and finished at `10.019M`. Its steady average from elapsed `220-490s` was about `403/sec`, its late pre-stop average was about `408/sec`, and drain averaged about `372/sec`; it crossed `10,000,000` at elapsed `442s` with `0` parser errors, retries, duplicates, or terminal markers. Validation passed summary recompute for `1-10019225`, sampled membership recompute, final-chunk S3 and coverage windows, and unchanged protected D2 Redis counts. This established PVE34 as the best practical fixed Nyx profile for that data band and showed that the limiter was DB/write coordination rather than fetch or JSON, with idle capacity still available. The immediate historical cleanup candidate was to demote or rate-limit status-only `parser_state.latest_parsed` writes.

The later durable autonomy evidence superseded fixed PVE34 worker identity and fixed short chunks as the operating model. Clean alpha runs exceeded `1k/sec`—best current-code alpha avg `1083.1 PGCR/sec`, steady `1122.9/sec`, final/max `1201.8/sec`; a no-special-fetch 2M alpha averaged `1056.4/sec` and `1092.8/sec` over its last half—while gamma S3-source evidence averaged `2141.3/sec`, steady `2243.0/sec`, final/max `2469.0/sec`. Live scenarios proved fetch should scale according to conditions: sustained `760ms` latency drove fetch to `128`; forced-lag slow edge reduced fetch/retry to floor `4`; healthy runs could pass through, settle at, fall below, or recover upward from `112`, so `112` was removed as a policy concept. Current policy therefore uses learned priors, measured fetch counts, batch `128` as a keeper ceiling rather than a law, fixed-budget DB rebalancing one worker at a time with accept/rollback and scenario-specific bad-trial memory, and rollup high-water only as a safety brake. PVE34 remains valid historical evidence about one Nyx write-pressure shape, not a universal autonomous setting.

answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. The framing correction expands it beyond learned-memory retrieval: it must preserve the inspectable state needed to resume, advance, verify, and hand off real work. Obsidian is a prototype corpus and human-readable projection, not the canonical product or storage boundary. Accordingly, the original retrieval-readiness benchmark remains only a regression baseline; the expanded gate must demonstrate successful continuation and improved durable next state on representative real workloads.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer: an agent-first continuity product and protocol, not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval system, or memory database. Its purpose is to let agents learn, continue, and iteratively advance complex work across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff.

Beyond durable learned knowledge, Straylight must preserve the live, resumable state of work: goals, current state, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved or open questions, rejected paths or approaches, checkpoints, and resumable next actions. That state must remain inspectable and support reopening, querying, computation, revision, verification, checkpointing, and handoff so a later agent can understand how the state was reached, advance it under new evidence, and leave a better durable state behind. The authoritative evidence layer also preserves immutable source episodes, artifact versions, corrections, provenance, authority, valid time, and transaction time; summaries, embeddings, indexes, context packs, and consolidated memory are derived aids rather than truth boundaries.

Obsidian is not the product boundary because Straylight's primary interaction model is agent-first rather than a human filing interface. Metis and its Obsidian vault organize the human knowledge base and provide a representative prototype and evaluation corpus; Markdown notes are useful human projections, prototype inputs, and export formats. Raw Markdown is not assumed to be Straylight's only or canonical storage representation, and full source and artifact access—not a particular notes application—remains part of the work substrate.

The first benchmark was too narrow because it evaluated retrieval readiness rather than the corrected product objective: 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items over 44 non-private notes, comparing direct full-file access, one-shot BM25 top-k, and a minimal deterministic Memory Workspace. It exercised `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read`, but left model-directed `memory.compute` and `memory.verify` untested; policy 0.2 and one-shot top-k each passed 17 of 20 cases, while top-k recovered 48 of 53 evidence items versus 46 of 53 for the workspace and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932. Thus the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated, policy 0.2 was frozen only as a retrieval regression baseline, and its tuned result is not holdout evidence. The expanded primary gate must compare direct filesystem search/range reads/scripts, an agent-first workspace with model-directed `open`, `query`, `read`, `compute`, `verify`, checkpoint, and revision behavior, and fixed handoff/context packs. On untouched holdout work it must prove that a fresh agent can correctly resume, iterate after constraints change, compute over quantitative artifacts, reason about time, supersession, and contradictions, inspect full sources, verify before acting, continue incidents and operational learning, and produce correct durable handoff and next-state artifacts. Required representative workloads are Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning—including booked-versus-proposed state—and Straylight's own evolving design. Correctness, completeness, evidence-chain recall, temporal accuracy, contradiction handling, source fidelity, project continuation, reasoning quality, durable-state quality, and ability to iterate outrank latency and cost; retrieval-only scores remain a regression lane rather than product proof.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer: an agent-first continuity substrate spanning research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval product, or memory database.

Beyond learned memory, Straylight must preserve the live state of work: evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, provenance, corrections, versions, and the next safe action. A later agent must be able to resume the work, inspect how its state was reached, revise it when evidence changes, verify it, and leave a better durable state behind.

Straylight is the portable agent context and durable-work product built over such material; raw Markdown is neither its required canonical interaction model nor necessarily its canonical or sole storage representation.
